summary: Creates points and polygons from parameters, DAT tables, or an existing input, making it useful for explicit point extraction, hand-built connection lists, and procedural boundary stitching.

key_params.name: pointdat
key_params.note: Table DAT path for point data; unnamed first columns map to x, y, z, and w

key_params.name: namedattribs
key_params.note: Enable named point attributes such as P, N, Cd, uv, and extra single-float columns

key_params.name: point0pos
key_params.note: Position for a point entry; can use constants or expressions

key_params.name: method
key_params.note: Choose group-based or pattern-based polygon creation

key_params.name: polydat
key_params.note: Table DAT path for polygon point-number rows and closed/open flags

key_params.name: poly0pattern
key_params.note: Connection-list pattern for polygon point order

common_gotchas: Turn off Compute Normals when the point table supplies N(0), N(1), and N(2).
Connection-list patterns are point-number based, so reversed ranges, exclusions, and '*' can create surprising vertex order.
Points added to an existing source are appended to the end of the point list.
key_concepts: Add SOP creates or appends points and polygons from parameters, DAT tables, or an existing SOP input.
Point DATs can use named attributes such as P, N, Cd, and uv, while unnamed first columns map to x, y, z, and w.
Polygon DAT rows and pattern strings are point-number connection lists, so vertex order is explicit and pattern-driven.
Post-processing options such as removing unused points and computing normals should match whether the input tables already provide normals.
